chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man says to you, 'Buy for me', do not give him from what is with you, even if that which is with you is better than it.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette when buying something for someone else according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a key principle in commercial etiquette (adab al-tijarah) to prevent ambiguity (gharar) and preserve the dignity of the buyer. By not handing over the item directly from one's possession, the transaction is clearly distinguished from a gift, ensuring that the buyer assumes full ownership and responsibility for the purchase. This practice reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on clarity in financial dealings to avoid disputes and maintain social harmony.
